baseline_models.focus_anchor: أَشَدُّ رَهْبَةً فِى صُدُورِهِم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ ... لَا يَفْقَهُونَ
baseline_models.mechanism: The comparative intensifies a constrictive fear located inside the chest and causally links its misordering of human and divine objects to failed understanding.

activation_trace.role: Strength and firmness supply the pressure scale expressed by the comparative أَشَدُّ.
Fear with contraction gives the intensified pressure its inward affective character.
The bodily chest localizes rather than merely names the fear.
Failure to grasp a matter explains the distorted ranking of feared objects.

changed_reading.before: The addressees are simply more frightening to them than God.
changed_reading.after: The ayah diagnoses a pressure hierarchy inside their chests: immediate human threat contracts them more strongly because understanding fails to rank visible and divine agency correctly.

baseline_models.mechanism: The singular interior diagnosis is generalized as a property of a qawm: a collective is constituted around a shared failure to understand, and that failure governs what issues from its members' chests.

activation_trace.role: The chest as an origin of actions turns inward fear into a source of group behavior.
The worshipped one supplies the displaced reference point in the group's fear ranking.
A human collective makes the cognitive failure socially shared rather than merely private.
Lack of understanding is the stated mechanism holding the collective pattern together.

changed_reading.before: The final clause gives a generic reason: they are unintelligent people.
changed_reading.after: The final clause identifies a collective operating defect: shared non-understanding lets an inwardly misranked fear become the group's organizing principle.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier failed fortification sequence relocates the decisive breach from walls to the interior: supposed preventing power collapses, terror is cast into hearts, and the occupants' own hands ruin their houses. The chest in 59:13 therefore reads as an inner fortification whose capture by proximate human fear converts hidden divine overthrow into self-defeating action.

activation_trace.role: Constrictive fear is the interior force whose downstream action the context makes visible.
The chest as an origin of action supplies the inner site from which fear can issue as conduct.
Protective power thought inaccessible establishes the failed defense model.
Preservation inside an encircling fort gives the exterior container that the chest internally echoes.
Casting something from a distance supplies the entry of terror into the defended interior.
The heart identifies the breached interior core rather than an exterior military position.
Fear and panic provide the earlier affective event that 59:13 anatomizes and compares.
Ruined habitation supplies the outward consequence of the interior breach.
What the hands earn makes self-destruction the behavioral output of captured fear.

structural_cues: 59:2 moves from confidence in enclosing fortresses to terror in hearts and then to houses destroyed by their occupants' own hands.
59:13 again places fear in an interior body-space and explicitly contrasts proximate human fear with God.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies failed forts, inwardly cast terror, and self-ruin; I infer that the chest is an inner fortification and that fear is the arrow from breach to action. A live alternative is that the two interiors are parallel descriptions without a transferred fortress mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Their inward fear of the believers is merely stronger than their fear of God.
changed_reading.after: Their chest is the breached inner fortress: fear of the believers is the immediate pressure through which an uncalculated divine defeat becomes self-defeating behavior.

context_deltas.mechanism: The neighboring positive community empties its chests of possessive need, prefers others despite privation, seeks protection from grasping selfishness, and prays that hearts remain free of concealed rancor. Against that interior economy, the fear occupying the chests in 59:13 is not neutral physiology but a rival allocation of the action-generating interior.

activation_trace.role: The chest as the source of action anchors the contrast between two interior economies.
Failed understanding explains why fear rather than discernment governs the interior.
The repeated chest is explicitly tested for what does or does not arise within it.
A need whose trace does not remain in the chest supplies the image of an interior cleared of possessive claim.
Choosing another over oneself turns the cleared interior into outward social action.
Grasping refusal is the counter-pressure from which the self must be guarded.
The heart continues the packet's mapping of morally consequential interior space.
Latent rancor in the chest shows that an inward occupant can organize relations even while hidden.

structural_cues: 59:9 and 59:13 repeat صُدُورِهِم while assigning sharply different contents and outcomes to that interior.
59:9-10 sequence absence of inward claim, preference for others, protection from selfish grasping, and removal of hidden rancor.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies contrasting contents of chests and hearts plus their social outputs; I infer an interior allocation mechanism in which what occupies the chest governs action. The alternative is that صدر is only a conventional idiom for private feeling.

changed_reading.before: The chest is simply the bodily location where fear is felt.
changed_reading.after: The chest is contested moral capacity: one community clears it of self-claim, while this group lets proximate fear occupy it and organize conduct because it does not understand.

context_deltas.mechanism: Promised support resolves into no support and turned backs; the next ayah exposes an apparent gathering whose hearts are scattered, even while their force among themselves is intense. Fear in 59:13 is thus an operational solvent of coalition: it converts social proximity and martial intensity into retreat, enclosure, and inward division.

activation_trace.role: Intensity in the focus provides the force whose social effect the surrounding sequence reveals.
Constrictive fear supplies the pressure that interrupts collective action.
The named collective anchors the reading in social rather than merely individual behavior.
Non-understanding supplies the focus ayah's explanation for failed coordination.
Repeated aid and its negation expose support as the coalition's failed function.
Turning away converts pledged nearness into operational abandonment.
Showing the back makes fear's directional output literal retreat.
Gathering dispersed parts supplies the outward appearance of a unified coalition.
Overpowering force locates their genuine intensity within their own relations.
Repeated intensity links the focus comparison to their severe force among themselves.
Scattering reveals the interior reality concealed by apparent gathering.
The repeated collective label binds the adjacent explanatory clauses into one social diagnosis.
Reason as a restraint from ignorance parallels non-understanding and explains why gathering does not become coherence.

structural_cues: 59:12 ends with failed aid and turned backs; 59:13 names the fear pressure; 59:14 contrasts apparent gathering with scattered hearts.
59:13 and 59:14 repeat the causal formula قَوْمٌ لَا plus a cognition verb.
The intensity of fear in 59:13 is followed by the intensity of their force among themselves in 59:14.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies promised aid, retreat, apparent gathering, inward scattering, and repeated cognitive diagnoses; I infer that fear is the causal solvent linking those states. A live alternative is that each is a separate symptom of hypocrisy rather than one coordination mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The ayah reports a high level of private fear.
changed_reading.after: The ayah identifies the pressure that dissolves a coalition: fear of the believers converts promised solidarity and real intensity into retreat, enclosure, and scattered hearts.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context distinguishes professed God-fear from governing God-fear. A false promise of solidarity is followed by a speaker who invokes fear of God precisely while disavowing the person he induced. The comparison in 59:13 can therefore measure which fear actually controls allegiance and action, not which sacred vocabulary is uttered.

activation_trace.role: Fear with action-inducing contraction anchors the test in effective rather than verbal fear.
The worshipped one is the comparator whose named fear may or may not govern behavior.
Failure to understand permits speech about God and conduct under another pressure to diverge.
The explicit contradiction of truth marks pledged solidarity as speech without governing force.
Spoken utterance frames both inducement and subsequent self-exculpation as verbal acts.
Disavowal and distancing reveal what the professed fear of God accomplishes socially.
Fear anticipating harm supplies the explicit profession that can be tested against conduct.
Naming God inside the disavowal makes the gap between invoked and governing fear visible.

structural_cues: 59:11 labels promised support false, while 59:16 places an explicit claim of fearing God inside an act of abandonment.
59:13 compares fear objects in the chest rather than counting verbal references to either object.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies false pledges and a God-fear utterance used during disavowal; I infer an operational test in which governing fear is identified by conduct. The alternative is that 59:16's statement is only part of an analogy and does not characterize the actors around 59:13.

changed_reading.before: Fearing people more than God means they lack verbal acknowledgment of divine fear.
changed_reading.after: They may invoke God-fear, yet the stronger fear is the one that governs allegiance and action; the ayah exposes an operational hierarchy rather than a vocabulary deficit.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later exhortation defines sound cognition as a self inspecting what it has sent ahead, then describes forgetting God as recursively producing self-forgetting. The non-fiqh of 59:13 is therefore a temporal and reflexive failure: fixation on immediate human threat blocks both recognition of ultimate agency and audit of one's own future-bearing action.

activation_trace.role: Failure to understand anchors the contextual expansion from ignorance to failed self-recognition.
The source of action ties inward cognition to what the self sends forward.
Directing sight or insight toward an object supplies the missing practice of deliberate review.
The self as the thing itself makes the review reflexive rather than an assessment of outsiders.
Advancing something ahead gives present action a future-directed trajectory.
Intentional action makes cognition answerable to conduct rather than abstract knowledge alone.
Loss of remembrance supplies the recursive failure linking neglect of God to loss of self.
The worshipped one is the forgotten reference point whose displacement deforms self-knowledge.
The self as one's own identity is the object lost when remembrance fails.

structural_cues: 59:18 orders a self to inspect what it has advanced for tomorrow; 59:19 makes forgetting God lead to forgetting selves.
59:13 already joins a misdirected fear ranking to lack of understanding.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies self-review, future-directed action, and the God-forgetting/self-forgetting sequence; I infer that immediate threat fixation blocks that temporal self-audit. A live alternative is that non-fiqh is narrower tactical incomprehension and the later self-address begins a separate exhortation.

changed_reading.before: They fail to understand who is truly more fearsome.
changed_reading.after: Their fear reveals failed self-audit: absorbed by immediate human threat, they lose the divine reference point, fail to see what their own actions send ahead, and thereby lose coherent knowledge of themselves.

context_deltas.mechanism: The mountain image differentiates fears by their transformations rather than merely their quantities. Human-directed رهبة contracts inside chests and contributes to hiding and social fracture; God-directed خشية makes even elevated solidity lower itself and split open. The comparative أَشَدُّ thus marks misdirected responsiveness, not proof that the immediate human threat has greater ultimate power.

activation_trace.role: Strength and solidity make the focus comparative available for a material transformation contrast.
Constrictive fear supplies the inward human-directed response being contrasted.
God as worshipped comparator anchors the second direction of fear.
An elevated solid mass supplies the maximal material test case for responsiveness.
Lowering and submission give divine awe a directional outcome unlike defensive contraction.
A fissure opening in something hard renders awe as transformation of solidity.
Fear joined with awe and reverence identifies the God-directed response mode.
The same divine comparator explicitly receives the mountain's awe.

structural_cues: 59:13 compares رهبة directed toward humans and God; 59:21 depicts خشية directed toward God.
The packet moves from scattered hearts behind fortifications to a solid mountain imagined as lowered and fissured.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two fear lexemes, their objects, and different bodily or material outcomes; I infer a contrast of transformations rather than a flat synonymy. The alternative is that the mountain is an independent parable about revelation with no backward differentiation of 59:13's fear.

changed_reading.before: The verse only says that one fear is quantitatively greater than another.
changed_reading.after: The comparison exposes wrongly directed responsiveness: fear of people contracts and fragments, whereas awe of God would make even hard solidity yield and open.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing names place the hidden chest under comprehensive knowledge, witness, care, sovereignty, and overpowering might. The group's error is therefore perspectival: visible human force dominates its interior calculation while the authority encompassing both hidden and witnessed realities is treated as less operative.

activation_trace.role: The action-generating chest is the hidden domain whose apparent privacy the closing names qualify.
The divine comparator is unfolded by the later cluster of names and powers.
Non-understanding anchors the failure to integrate hidden and visible agency.
Disclosure to the knower supplies comprehensive cognition that counters the group's non-fiqh.
What is concealed from eyes includes the inward fear-space that humans may misread as private.
Presence with observation completes the hidden/manifest scope of divine knowledge.
Kingship and sovereignty oppose the group's overvaluation of immediate social power.
Witnessing care makes the inward domain continuously attended rather than strategically hidden.
Overpowering might supplies the ultimate power that their fear calculation underweights.

structural_cues: 59:13 locates the ranking in chests; 59:22 immediately defines divine knowledge across hidden and witnessed domains.
59:23 follows knowledge with sovereignty, watchful care, and overpowering might.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an inward location followed by names of comprehensive knowledge and authority; I infer that the closing names audit the group's hidden threat model. The alternative is that the name sequence is doxological closure without a specific backward link to the chests.

changed_reading.before: God is one item on the same fear scale as the believers.
changed_reading.after: The scale itself is cognitively malformed: a hidden chest privileges visible social force over the sovereign knower who encompasses hidden and witnessed reality alike.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the anatomical chest-bone branch of رهب rather than the ordinary fear branch. It remains anchored in رَهْبَةً beside صُدُور and gains a material analogue from the hard mountain splitting in 59:21. Downstream prose should present it only as a load-bearing body analogy, never as a claim that رَهْبَة lexically means a chest bone here.

activation_trace.role: The projecting bone of the chest makes fear imaginable at a load-bearing anatomical ridge.
The literal chest keeps the anatomical activation attached to the focus construction.
Strength and solidity supply the load carried by this materialized interior.
A raised solid mass provides a larger-scale analogue for a load-bearing chest structure.
The opening fissure suggests what happens when a rigid structure can no longer bear its governing pressure.

changed_reading.before: Fear is an emotion contained in the chest.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, fear occupies the chest's load-bearing structure: the group's apparent hardness is internally stressed, anticipating the image of solidity that yields by splitting open.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is branch-distant because it activates رهب as worship intensified by dread and pairs it with a rare monastic side branch under قدس. It remains anchored in رَهْبَةً and the explicit God comparison, while 59:16 supplies a performed claim of fearing God. Downstream prose should label it a lexical resonance about pseudo-devotion, not identify the group as monks or derive doctrine from the قدس side branch.

activation_trace.role: Devotion intensified by dread opens the possibility that fear can mimic a religious discipline.
Worship and the worshipped one anchor the exploratory devotional contrast in the focus.
A spoken fear of anticipated harm shows divine-fear language operating inside self-protective abandonment.
The rare monk-associated branch supplies a deliberately contained lexical resonance with the focus root's monastic branch.

changed_reading.before: Their stronger human fear is simply irreligious fear.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, human-directed dread can become pseudo-devotional: it disciplines allegiance with the form-like intensity of piety while displacing the worshipped object that should govern it.

strongest_changes: The chest became an inner fortification breached by fear, with self-defeating action as the breach's outward result.
The comparative fear became a coalition mechanism that turns apparent gathering and pledged aid into retreat and scattered hearts.
Non-fiqh expanded from generic ignorance into failed future-directed self-audit and recursive self-forgetting.
The mountain contrast differentiated human-directed contraction from God-directed awe that makes solidity yield and open.
summary.what_was_special: The packet repeatedly coupled interior containers with social outputs: hearts receive terror, chests can be cleared of possessive need or occupied by fear, hidden rancor shapes relations, and apparently gathered people remain inwardly scattered. The adjacent repetition of collective cognitive diagnoses in 59:13-14 made fear, group incoherence, and non-understanding one especially strong mechanism.
remaining_uncertainties: The mountain's awe may be an independent revelation parable rather than a deliberate backward contrast with 59:13.
The inner-fortress and load-bearing chest readings depend on spatial and material transfer beyond ordinary idiom.
The performed-fear model may characterize the analogical speaker of 59:16 more directly than the group addressed around 59:13.
